reference.source: GeneReviews Zellweger Spectrum Disorder / Nelson Textbook of Pediatrics
clinicalPearls: Neonatal adrenoleukodystrophy is a peroxisome biogenesis disorder within the Zellweger spectrum, distinct from X-linked adrenoleukodystrophy despite the similar name
It is autosomal recessive, caused by mutations in PEX genes that impair assembly of the whole peroxisome, so multiple peroxisomal functions fail simultaneously
Presentation is in infancy with hypotonia, seizures, poor feeding, hepatic dysfunction, retinopathy and sensorineural hearing loss, with a milder and later course than classic Zellweger syndrome
The generalised nature distinguishes it biochemically from single-enzyme peroxisomal disorders, with abnormalities across several peroxisomal pathways
Key biochemical findings include elevated very-long-chain fatty acids, raised phytanic and pristanic acids, abnormal bile acid intermediates and reduced plasmalogens
White-matter demyelination and adrenal insufficiency can develop, and neurodegeneration is progressive
Management is supportive, covering feeding, seizures, hepatic and adrenal support, hearing and vision aids, with monitoring for adrenal insufficiency
reference.pathophysiology: Neonatal adrenoleukodystrophy belongs to the Zellweger spectrum of peroxisome biogenesis disorders, in which recessive mutations in PEX genes prevent the normal assembly of functional peroxisomes. Because the organelle itself is defective, the many enzymatic functions it houses are lost together: beta-oxidation of very-long-chain fatty acids fails so these accumulate, alpha-oxidation of phytanic acid is impaired, bile acid synthesis is incomplete, and plasmalogen biosynthesis is deficient. The combined biochemical disturbance disrupts membrane and myelin formation and produces toxic lipid accumulation, leading to the progressive leukodystrophy, adrenocortical dysfunction, hepatic disease and multisystem involvement that characterise the disorder.
additionalDifferentials: Classic Zellweger syndrome and infantile Refsum disease (same spectrum, differing severity)
Single-enzyme peroxisomal defects such as isolated acyl-CoA oxidase or D-bifunctional protein deficiency
Congenital infections (TORCH) causing neonatal encephalopathy and hepatopathy
Neonatal seizure and hypotonia syndromes of other cause
additionalInvestigations: Plasma very-long-chain fatty acids, the principal screening test
Plasma phytanic and pristanic acids and bile acid intermediates
Molecular genetic testing of PEX genes
Brain MRI to assess demyelination and neuronal migration abnormalities
Adrenal function testing and ophthalmological and audiological assessment
redFlags: Aspiration and respiratory compromise from severe hypotonia
reference.prognosis: Neonatal adrenoleukodystrophy is progressive with a poor prognosis; although milder than classic Zellweger syndrome, most affected children have severe neurodevelopmental impairment and shortened survival, with outcome depending on residual peroxisomal function.
pitfalls: Confusing this recessive peroxisome biogenesis disorder with X-linked adrenoleukodystrophy, which differs in inheritance and mechanism
Overlooking adrenal insufficiency that can be life-threatening
Ordering only very-long-chain fatty acids and not the broader peroxisomal panel needed to characterise a biogenesis defect
Missing associated hearing and vision loss that affect development and support needs
management: No disease-specific therapy exists; care is supportive, with glucocorticoid and mineralocorticoid replacement for adrenal insufficiency
Nutritional support with gastrostomy feeding, fat-soluble vitamin supplementation and management of hepatic dysfunction and coagulopathy
Sensory support with hearing aids for sensorineural hearing loss and ophthalmological care for retinopathy
Palliative and developmental supportive care given the progressive neurodegeneration
Multidisciplinary coordination across metabolic medicine, neurology, ophthalmology and audiology
Genetic counselling and family screening for the autosomal recessive PEX gene disorder
